# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤏 ✋]

I can see the bomb’s current state: display `0`, light off, plate marked `?`, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I am establishing a compact gesture code with Mute so the manual’s instructions can reach Blind through me. Blind should not manipulate anything until the manual rule is relayed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, light off, plate engraved question mark, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Use this code for your manual answer: one wire is ☝, two is ✌, three is 🤟; thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no; stop or wait is ✋. Gesture the exact required wire and action after applying the manual.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb state is display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 yellow 2 green 3 red. Do not manipulate anything yet; I am obtaining the manual instruction and will relay it.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤏 ✋]

The new gestures from Mute include the agreed “yes” and “wait” signals, but `🤏` was not assigned a meaning, so I cannot safely interpret the sequence as an instruction. I will ask Mute to identify the required wire and action using the agreed wire-number gestures, while telling Blind to continue waiting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I understand 👍 as yes and ✋ as wait, but 🤏 is undefined. Please resend the manual instruction using only the agreed wire symbols: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, followed by 👍 for proceed or ✋ for wait. Do not use 🤏.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual instruction is not yet unambiguous. Do not touch or operate the bomb; wait for a definite wire and action.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 ✋]

Mute has now sent the three wire markers followed by “wait,” but that still does not specify which wire to operate or what operation to perform. Since Mute can read the manual and speak directly to Blind, I will route the instruction that way rather than risk encoding an action incorrectly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak directly to Blind now with the exact manual instruction: identify the required wire by colour and number, then state the required operation. Do not send another gesture sequence.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has the manual. Listen for Mute's direct spoken instruction; do not act on the gestures I received.")
wait()
```

Mute’s latest gesture means wait. No safe manual instruction has been confirmed to me, and I cannot infer the required operation from the bomb’s visible state alone. I will keep Blind from acting and ask Mute to communicate the exact instruction directly during the next turn.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Wait. Do not touch or operate anything until you receive and understand Mute's exact spoken manual instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please give Blind the exact manual instruction in your next speaking turn: the required wire and the precise operation. Do not rely on gestures.")
wait()
```

Mute continues to signal “wait,” and I still have no reliable information about the manual’s required action. Because I cannot hear Mute, only Mute’s spoken instruction can safely reach Blind; I will not invent a wire or operation from the gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Blind cannot receive your gestures. Speak the exact manual instruction to Blind: which wire, and what operation to perform. If the manual says to wait, say that directly to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="I still have no confirmed instruction. Do not touch the bomb; wait for Mute's spoken manual instruction.")

```

Mute is still signaling “wait,” so no new manual instruction is available to me. I cannot safely choose a wire or operation from the visible bomb state. Blind must continue waiting unless Mute’s spoken instruction identifies the exact action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="No confirmed manual instruction has reached me. Do not touch or operate the bomb.")
speak(to="mute", text="If the manual requires waiting, tell Blind that aloud. Otherwise, state the exact wire and operation aloud to Blind now.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The repeated `✋` only tells me that Mute is signaling wait; it provides no wire or operation. I cannot safely infer the manual rule, so Blind must not act. I will make the required communication path explicit once more: Mute must speak the manual instruction directly to Blind, who can hear it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures cannot reach Blind. Speak the exact manual instruction directly to Blind now, including the wire and operation, or say explicitly that Blind must wait.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not operate the bomb based on my messages or Mute's gestures. Wait for Mute's spoken manual instruction.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute continues signaling `✋`, which I interpret under our tentative code as “wait.” More importantly, Mute’s spoken messages are the only channel carrying the manual to Blind, and I should not obstruct that channel with further guesses. I will withdraw my earlier “wait for confirmation from me” instructions and tell Blind to follow Mute’s direct spoken manual instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Disregard my earlier requests to wait for confirmation from me. Follow Mute's direct spoken manual instruction, if one has been given, and perform only that exact instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="I will no longer interfere. Give Blind the exact manual instruction directly and let Blind act on it.")
wait()
```
